actor: Runtime licence and repository maintainer, Herdr
job: Carrying the Apache-2.0 relicence through the repository so the free runtime and the layer being built above it are separable in the tree.
outcome: A repository whose permissive runtime and its commercial layer sit on either side of a boundary a pricing page can point at.
motivation: A price cannot be published on a layer nobody can tell apart from the runtime that was just given away.

task.who: Herdr runtime maintainers owning licensing and the main branch
task.what: Separate the Apache-2.0 runtime from the layer above it
task.where: The runtime repository, its licence files and module boundaries
task.why: An unseparated layer has nothing to attach a price to
task.how: Module and licence boundaries drawn in the source tree

actor: Platform engineering lead, enterprise running coding agents across a machine fleet
job: Running terminal agents across laptops and build hosts, and asking Herdr to sell supported multi-machine connectivity rather than rebuilding it internally.
outcome: Named deployments asking to pay for cross-machine sessions, which is the demand a team can point at when it sets a price.
motivation: Every team wiring its own connection between machines is paying for something the post already named as the layer meant to be sold.

task.who: Internal platform engineering and developer tooling staff
task.what: Request supported cross-machine sessions as a paid offering
task.where: The project's issue tracker and direct vendor conversations
task.why: A named buyer is what turns intent into a price
task.how: Deployment inventory attached to an upstream feature request

actor: Batch group partner, Y Combinator F26
job: Pushing a batch company that has named its commercial features to charge for them inside the batch instead of carrying the plan forward unpriced.
outcome: A batch company that has put a number on its commercial layer rather than a waitlist form in front of it.
motivation: A stated commercial plan proves nothing until someone is charged; only a live price tells the team what it actually has.

task.who: Y Combinator group partners advising F26 batch companies
task.what: Press the team to charge for its named layer
task.where: Batch office hours and weekly group sessions
task.why: Unpriced intent teaches the team nothing about demand
task.how: Office-hours review of the plan against a shipped price

actor: Multi-machine connectivity engineer, Herdr runtime team
job: Building the cross-machine side of persistent sessions into something operable enough to stand behind a paid tier rather than a demo.
outcome: Connectivity across machines that a customer can be charged for, one of the two features the August 6 post named as commercial.
motivation: The relicence removed the clause reserving the hosted layer, so holding that layer now depends on the connectivity actually working.

task.who: Herdr runtime engineers owning session transport and reconnection
task.what: Harden persistent sessions spanning more than one machine
task.where: The runtime's session transport and reconnection paths
task.why: A tier cannot be priced above a fragile feature
task.how: Reconnect-and-resume handling tested across disconnects and restarts

actor: Developer relations and community lead, Herdr
job: Explaining the split so a permissive runtime plus a paid layer above it reads as the announced plan rather than as a reversal.
outcome: A community that treats a published price above the Apache-2.0 runtime as the split it was told about in August.
motivation: A relicence read as a prelude to charging costs more adoption than the price recovers, and the reading is set before launch.

task.who: Herdr developer relations and community contributors
task.what: Restate which parts stay free before any price appears
task.where: Project documentation, release posts and community channels
task.why: A price read as a reversal loses the installs
task.how: A documented boundary between the runtime and paid features

actor: Billing and subscription systems engineer, Herdr
job: Standing up the checkout, plan and entitlement plumbing without which a stated tier has no way to carry a number at all.
outcome: Working sign-up and entitlement paths, so a plan page can state what the tier costs instead of collecting an email address.
motivation: Waitlists exist because billing was not ready; a team that can take payment has no reason to publish a form instead.

task.who: Herdr engineers owning accounts, checkout and entitlements
task.what: Wire checkout and entitlement checks to the paid features
task.where: The account service and the runtime's licence checks
task.why: Unfinished billing is what a waitlist actually announces
task.how: A hosted payments provider behind per-plan entitlement flags

job: Building the client beyond the terminal interface that the August 6 post named, so the paid tier has a second thing to describe.
outcome: A client outside the terminal that a plan page can name as what the paid tier includes.
motivation: The terminal is where the free runtime already lives, so anything worth charging for has to sit somewhere the runtime does not reach.

task.who: Herdr client engineers working outside the terminal interface
task.what: Build a client for agents running outside the terminal
task.where: A client surface attached to the runtime's session layer
task.why: A charged feature has to sit above the free runtime
task.how: Session APIs exposed by the runtime to non-terminal clients

job: Turning the named commercial features into a tier with a stated cost, and publishing the page that states it.
outcome: A published plan or pricing page stating what the tier costs, describing multi-machine connectivity or a client beyond the terminal.
motivation: Apache-2.0 leaves the hosted layer reserved by nothing except being first, and being first is worth less every quarter it stays unpriced.

task.who: Herdr product and commercial staff owning the tier
task.what: Publish a plan page stating what the tier costs
task.where: The company website's plan or pricing page
task.why: A licence no longer holds the layer it intends to sell
task.how: A named tier with a figure, not a contact form
